body:
`FileSystemDirectoryHandle` objects can be stored in IndexedDB via `idb-keyval` directly — Chrome serializes them. On page load, `queryPermission({mode: "read"})` tells us whether the previously granted permission still holds. If not, `requestPermission` must be called synchronously in response to a user gesture. So after a fresh Chrome restart, the user clicks "Reconnect folder" on the sidebar → that click provides the user-activation token that lets the permission prompt show.

Handles persist across sessions. Permission grants persist within a session but are re-requested after browser restart. This is a Chrome security constraint, not something our code can bypass.

Session-live file handles (per-file `FileSystemFileHandle` for every renderable file inside a picked folder) are kept in a plain in-memory `Map` (`sessionHandles` singleton). Not serialized because that's cheap to rebuild — one directory walk after reconnect.
